Confusion Matrix Type

Source: R/type_confusion.R
type_confusion.Rd

Creates publication-ready confusion matrix heatmaps for classification results. Cell fill encodes the count, cell text shows the number of observations, and the caption reports accuracy (and, for 2x2 tables, a Fisher exact test p-value). Inspired by cnsplots' confusionplot().

Usage

type_confusion(
  add_pvalue = FALSE,
  show_accuracy = TRUE,
  color_low = "#F7F7F7",
  color_high = "#B2182B",
  text_color = "white",
  label_size = 4.2,
  show_totals = FALSE
)

Arguments

add_pvalue

Add a Fisher exact test p-value to the caption for 2x2 tables (default FALSE).

show_accuracy

Show classification accuracy in the caption (default TRUE).

color_low

Low end of the count color gradient (default "#F7F7F7").

color_high

High end of the count color gradient (default "#B2182B").

text_color

Color of the count labels (default "white").

label_size

Size of the count labels (default 4.2).

show_totals

Show row/column marginal totals (default FALSE).

Value

A cliplot_type object for use with cliplot.

Details

Use the formula interface cliplot(truth ~ predicted, data, type = "confusion") where y is the ground-truth variable and x the predicted variable. A data frame with exactly two factor/character columns is also accepted directly.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
cliplot(truth ~ predicted, data = predictions, type = "confusion")
cliplot(truth ~ predicted, data = predictions,
        type = type_confusion(add_pvalue = TRUE))
} # }
